Detailed logs, for reporting a problem. What is logged is set by the debug_* lines in xerenge.conf.
The game starts its next frame while the GPU still draws this one. Faster; once showed a black frame now and then.
The frame goes to the GPU before the game waits for the display to take the next one, so the two overlap. About 50 -> 60 fps in a race on a Ryzen 5 4500U.
Only the vertex data each shader reads goes to the GPU, not a layout wide enough for every shader. Less memory traffic; turn off if models look broken.
Skip the faces the game culls itself, as the console does. Experimental.
Draw the frame at this size and scale it onto the window. 1280x720 is the size the game renders at on the console.
Frames per second in the top left corner.
The system Vulkan driver is recent enough (1.2 or newer).
The system Vulkan driver is below 1.2, which the game needs. Load a Mesa Turnip driver package (.zip, the kind emulators use).
Could not read the driver package: %1$s
That is not a driver package: no meta.json naming a library, and not a single .so file.
Your name online: up to 15 letters, digits, - and _.
Turns the online menus on. Every copy of the game on your network runs a lobby of its own; the games one player creates show up for the others, and any player can host.
empty: no server, local multiplayer only
The host or IP of a lobby server of your own (the release carries one). With an address the game plays online through that server, and local multiplayer is off.
Playing online through the server %1$s; local multiplayer is off.
Local multiplayer finds the games of the other copies on your network. To play through a server, enter its address.

Translucent pad buttons over the game: a stick on the left half (where the thumb lands is its centre), RT and LT for accelerating and braking, A B X Y, LB RB, Back and Start. A connected pad still works.
How much of the picture the buttons cover.
